officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirmed --test-name-pattern / -t is documented as a REGEX filter ('Run only tests with a name that matches the given regex'), so test names containing + or parentheses must be escaped inside every -t oracle. The docs do not document the zero-match case at all, so the measured behaviour recorded in the issue ('matched 0 tests', non-success) is the only evidence available: every -t oracle in this PRD therefore keeps the mandatory nonzero-pass-count conjunct and never degrades to a bare exit-code check. No breaking changes or deprecations affecting bun test filtering.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [src/supervisor/plan-escalation.ts:89]: The positive read path of the new exhaustedBudget field is untested. No test anywhere writes a persisted marker CONTAINING exhaustedBudget and reads it back through readPlanEscalatedMarker: test/supervisor/plan/plan-escalation.test.ts only covers the legacy five-field marker (asserting the field is undefined), and every other PlanEscalatedMarker in the suite (test/unit/status-projection.test.ts, test/unit/status-diagnostics.test.ts) is an in-memory literal that never crosses the read boundary. A regression that always dropped the field at read (e.g. `const exhaustedBudget = undefined`) would leave all 5755 tests green, yet readPlanEscalatedMarker (src/commands/status.ts:657) is the only production consumer of the persisted marker, so the operator-facing purpose of US-003 would be silently defeated. Add a round-trip test asserting a marker written with exhaustedBudget: 'auditor' reads back with the field intact, plus the adversarial case that an unknown value (e.g. 'bogus') is dropped rather than trusted (the branch the comment at :87-88 claims).

userStories.title: Carry the block origin on the audit-blocked plan result
userStories.description: As the plan supervisor, I need every audit-blocked result to declare whether it came from the deterministic oracle lint or from the auditor, so the re-plan driver can budget the two independently instead of folding them into one indistinguishable counter.
acceptanceCriteria: The audit-blocked member of PlanPhaseResult (src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:277) carries a REQUIRED origin field typed 'oracle-lint' | 'auditor'. runOracleLintCheck (:1003) constructs it with 'oracle-lint' and the auditor BLOCK return in runPlanWorkerSequence (:1344) constructs it with 'auditor'. Required, not optional: every construction site must declare provenance, so a future one cannot silently default to the wrong budget. [oracle: file-assert grep -q "origin: 'oracle-lint'" src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts && grep -q "origin: 'auditor'" src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts]

A test named EXACTLY 'audit-blocked carries origin oracle-lint for a lint block and auditor for an auditor BLOCK' is added to test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts and passes. It drives runPlanPhase twice through the existing makeOpts harness: once with readPrdContentFn injected to return the lint-FAILING BROKEN_PRD fixture (expect origin 'oracle-lint', auditor never spawned) and once with the lint-clean CLEAN_PRD fixture plus a BLOCK verdict (expect origin 'auditor'). [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts -t 'audit-blocked carries origin oracle-lint for a lint block and auditor for an auditor BLOCK' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']

This story is discriminator-only: the re-plan loop still counts both origins against MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS, so the ADR-0040 invariance pin (lint blocks every round, auditor never spawned) stays green untouched. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts -t 'AC4: exhausting re-plan rounds on a persistently-broken oracle escalates via writeEscalationMarkerFn, auditor never spawned' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]

Tests pass (bun test) with zero failures. Expressed as a zero-failure assertion, never a pass-count floor, because a pinned pass count rots on every added test (CAM-447). [oracle: out=$(bun test 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']
The lint spine stays green. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts (PlanPhaseResult union member at :277, runOracleLintCheck at :994-1004, the auditor BLOCK return at :1344), test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts (BROKEN_PRD :87 / CLEAN_PRD :99 fixtures and the makeOpts harness already inject readPrdContentFn). GOTCHA: making origin REQUIRED breaks the audit-blocked object literal at test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-postaudit.test.ts:87 by construction; update that literal rather than weakening the field to optional. GOTCHA: runOracleLintCheck's return type is Extract<PlanPhaseResult, { kind: 'audit-blocked' }>, so the new field flows into it automatically once the union member changes. Design context: docs/adr/0052 ('Decision' paragraph) and the lint-origin BLOCK / auditor-origin BLOCK glossary entries in CONTEXT.md. Do NOT touch the round budgets in this story: US-002 owns them.

userStories.title: Budget oracle-lint and auditor re-plan rounds independently
userStories.description: As an operator whose PRD tripped the deterministic oracle lint, I need the lint round not to spend the auditor's correction budget, so that the auditor's findings always get at least one post-auditor correction round before the plan escalates.
acceptanceCriteria: A lint-origin block must not spend the auditor's correction budget: when round 1 is blocked by the oracle-lint and the following round's AUDITOR returns BLOCK, the run performs a further post-auditor correction round instead of escalating. Add a test to test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts named EXACTLY 'lint round 1 leaves the auditor budget intact and a post-auditor correction round still runs', driving runPlanPhaseWithReplan via the existing options-builder harness with readPrdContentFn injected to return a lint-FAILING prd on round 1 and a lint-clean prd on every later round, verdicts ordered [APPROVE, BLOCK, APPROVE], asserting the terminal kind is 'audit-approved' and that the auditor was spawned at least twice. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts -t 'lint round 1 leaves the auditor budget intact and a post-auditor correction round still runs' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']

The lint budget is introduced as a NEW exported constant (MAX_LINT_REPLAN_ROUNDS) while MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS keeps its name and its value of 2 and continues to mean the AUDITOR budget; the lint budget is independently bounded so a persistently broken oracle cannot spin the planner. [oracle: file-assert grep -qE 'export const MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS = 2' src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts && grep -qE 'export const MAX_LINT_REPLAN_ROUNDS' src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts]

The one test that codified the CAM-447 pathology as expected behaviour is REWRITTEN, never deleted: test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts:425 'mixed: round-1 lint-block then round-2 real auditor BLOCK both fold into the SAME escalation path' currently asserts that scenario escalates with roundsCompleted 2, which the new contract forbids. The replacement keeps a test whose name still begins with 'mixed: round-1 lint-block then round-2 real auditor BLOCK' and asserts the non-escalating outcome. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts -t 'mixed: round-1 lint-block then round-2 real auditor BLOCK' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']

INVARIANCE PIN, must stay GREEN: the pure-auditor path is behaviourally untouched, so the existing spawn-cycle pin keeps passing UNMODIFIED. A fix that merely raises or re-points MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS would satisfy the first criterion while breaking this one. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts -t 'escalation: exactly MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS planner\+auditor spawn cycles occur \(no 3rd round\)' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']

INVARIANCE PIN, must stay GREEN: when the lint blocks EVERY round the auditor is still NEVER spawned (ADR-0040) and the run still terminates. This is the constraint most likely to be inverted by a careless reading; the invariant is NOT 'the auditor must always run'. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts -t 'AC4: exhausting re-plan rounds on a persistently-broken oracle escalates via writeEscalationMarkerFn, auditor never spawned' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test) with zero failures. [oracle: out=$(bun test 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']
The lint spine stays green. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts (runPlanPhaseWithReplan at :1500, the single-counter init at :1507, the loop guard at :1509, and the POST-loop escalation branch at :1531), test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts (options-builder harness), test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts (the AC6 rewrite at :425). GOTCHA, enforcement point: the fix is NOT only the loop guard at :1509. After the loop exits, escalating requires that the budget matching the FINAL block's origin actually be exhausted; changing only the guard leaves the terminal wrong. GOTCHA, harness blind spot: runOracleLintCheck early-returns null when readPrdContentFn === undefined (:998), and EVERY existing test in plan-runner-replan.test.ts leaves it unset, which is why none of them touch the lint path today. A new test that forgets to inject it silently drives the auditor path and passes for the wrong reason; test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts is the only file that currently injects it and is the reference for the fixture shape. GOTCHA, harness side effect: the per-round verdict advances via roundIndex++ inside teardownPlanPanesFn (plan-runner-replan.test.ts:195-203), not inside the runner; any override of teardownPlanPanesFn must preserve that or every round reads verdict[0] forever. GOTCHA, bun -t is a regex (confirmed in officialDocsConsulted), so + and parentheses in a pinned test name must be escaped, as the spawn-cycle pin oracle already shows. Accepted cost, not a regression: worst-case planner spawns per plan call rise from MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS to MAX_LINT_REPLAN_ROUNDS + MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS; the independent bound is what keeps it finite. Three separate tests assert MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS === 2 (test/supervisor/plan/plan-replan.test.ts:99-101, test/plan-runner-in-progress-conflict.test.ts:211, and the spawn-cycle pin), which is why the lint budget must be a NEW constant. Do NOT absorb CAM-438 (lint over-fire): a perfectly precise lint would still be wrong to charge the auditor's budget. Design context: docs/adr/0052 'Decision' and 'Consequences'.

userStories.title: Name the exhausted budget on the escalation marker and event
userStories.description: As an operator reading a plan escalation, I need the durable marker and the plan-escalated event to say WHICH budget was exhausted, so I can tell a planner that cannot write valid oracles apart from a design the auditor keeps rejecting now that a bare roundsCompleted is ambiguous.
acceptanceCriteria: The durable escalation marker and the plan-escalated event each name the exhausted budget via an exhaustedBudget field typed 'oracle-lint' | 'auditor', added to PlanEscalatedMarker (src/supervisor/plan-escalation.ts:37-43), threaded through PlanEscalationWriterParams (src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:1422) and the writeMarker call (:1533-1538), and added to PlanEscalatedEventDetail (src/supervisor/events.ts:498-501) and the emitted detail (:1546-1552). Add a test to test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts named EXACTLY 'escalation marker and event name the exhausted budget'. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts -t 'escalation marker and event name the exhausted budget' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']

Separating the counters introduces no unbounded planner spin: a run whose oracle-lint blocks on EVERY round terminates as kind 'plan-escalated' with exhaustedBudget naming the oracle-lint budget, and total planner spawns across the call stay bounded by the sum of the two budgets. Add a test named EXACTLY 'lint budget is independently bounded and escalates naming the oracle-lint budget'. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts -t 'lint budget is independently bounded and escalates naming the oracle-lint budget' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']

Backward compatibility of the persisted marker: a .cam-plan-escalated.json written by an older binary, lacking exhaustedBudget, still parses instead of being rejected by the five-field shape guard at src/supervisor/plan-escalation.ts:66-81. The field is therefore optional at the read boundary even though it is always written. Add a test to test/supervisor/plan/plan-escalation.test.ts named EXACTLY 'a five-field marker without exhaustedBudget still round-trips'. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-escalation.test.ts -t 'a five-field marker without exhaustedBudget still round-trips' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']

The optionality is expressed in the type itself, not only in the guard, so existing PlanEscalatedMarker literals in status projection/diagnostics tests keep compiling. [oracle: file-assert grep -qE 'exhaustedBudget\?:' src/supervisor/plan-escalation.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test) with zero failures. [oracle: out=$(bun test 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']
The lint spine stays green. [oracle: bun run check:all]

findings.text: The positive read path of the new exhaustedBudget field is untested. No test anywhere writes a persisted marker CONTAINING exhaustedBudget and reads it back through readPlanEscalatedMarker: test/supervisor/plan/plan-escalation.test.ts only covers the legacy five-field marker (asserting the field is undefined), and every other PlanEscalatedMarker in the suite (test/unit/status-projection.test.ts, test/unit/status-diagnostics.test.ts) is an in-memory literal that never crosses the read boundary. A regression that always dropped the field at read (e.g. `const exhaustedBudget = undefined`) would leave all 5755 tests green, yet readPlanEscalatedMarker (src/commands/status.ts:657) is the only production consumer of the persisted marker, so the operator-facing purpose of US-003 would be silently defeated. Add a round-trip test asserting a marker written with exhaustedBudget: 'auditor' reads back with the field intact, plus the adversarial case that an unknown value (e.g. 'bogus') is dropped rather than trusted (the branch the comment at :87-88 claims).

Doc comments describing the escalation contract were left stale by the budget split, including the very block this diff edited. events.ts:494 still reads 'BLOCK->re-plan loop exhausts MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS without an APPROVE verdict' two lines above the newly added exhaustedBudget bullet that exists precisely because that is no longer the only escalation path. Same staleness at events.ts:72, src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:248 (plan-escalated kind doc), :1472 (writeEscalationMarkerFn seam doc: 'Invoked exactly once, when MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS consecutive audit-blocked rounds are exhausted'), :1523 (function headline: 'Drive runPlanPhase through up to MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS rounds'), :2161, src/supervisor/plan-escalation.ts:6 and :23, and src/commands/sidecar.ts:2396. In a codebase whose recorded lesson is that stale comments mislead decisions, a mechanical sweep of these sentences belongs in the same change that altered the behavior they describe.

PlanEscalationWriterParams = Omit<PlanEscalatedMarker, 'writtenAt'> inherits exhaustedBudget as OPTIONAL, so the writer seam does not force a future escalation site to declare which budget was exhausted, even though US-001 deliberately made the same discriminator REQUIRED on the audit-blocked result for exactly that reason. Consider `Omit<PlanEscalatedMarker, 'writtenAt' | 'exhaustedBudget'> & { exhaustedBudget: 'oracle-lint' | 'auditor' }` so optionality stays confined to the read boundary where backward compatibility actually needs it.

The planner-spawn bound is asserted only for the all-lint-blocked run, where the true bound is MAX_LINT_REPLAN_ROUNDS (2) but the assertion allows MAX_LINT_REPLAN_ROUNDS + MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS (4). An interleaved run (lint block, auditor block, lint block) is the case where the summed bound is actually load-bearing and is currently uncovered; a test driving alternating origins would pin the combined worst case the ADR calls out as the accepted cost.
